issues_confirmed.detail: avg_sentiment, min_sentiment and pct_negative_msgs are merged on order_id and fillna(0) for orders with no ticket - structurally identical to msg_count, which IS dropped by LEAKAGE_MAP['has_ticket']. The three sentiment columns are not. Counted from the data: 1204 tickets on 1204 distinct orders covering 1705 line-item rows, and all 1204 tickets have at least one customer message, so every positive row gets a real VADER score and all 68251 negatives are exactly 0.0. avg_sentiment != 0 implies has_ticket == 1 over 100% of the positive class. git show ec57f66 confirms the mechanism: the Phase 10 commit added the three columns to _build_joined and added three entries to FILTER_MAP, but did not touch LEAKAGE_MAP. has_ticket is absent from KEY_TARGETS (nn/evaluate.py:348-362) so no published figure is affected, but --target has_ticket is a supported call.

Carried from 2026-09-17, untouched. LEAKAGE_MAP['has_refund'] drops refund_reason but not size_issue / damaged_in_transit, which _engineer_features builds as pure functions of refund_reason. refund_reason is 'none' on every non-refunded row, so size_issue==1 implies has_refund==1. Recounted from data/refunds.csv this run: size_too_small 1284 + size_too_large 1109 + damaged_in_transit 752 = 3145/5843 = 53.8% of refunds, matching the reported recall 0.5461 (REPORT.md:170). REPORT.md:180 lists those two flags as the #1 (delta 0.794) and #2 (delta 0.278) features. The 'leakage-free' AUC 0.8436 at REPORT.md:461 is inflated.

Carried from 2026-09-17, untouched, and independently recounted this run. _load_refunds parses refund_line_items into refund_variant_ids on line 68 and discards the column on line 69, then merges refunds on order_id onto a line-item-grain table. From the CSVs: 5843 refunds, no order refunded twice, every refund_line_items array has length exactly 1, and those orders contain 10025 line items - so 4182 rows (41.7% of positives) are mislabelled. Matches REPORT.md:174 'Positive rate (actual) 14.33%' = 10025/69956; the true line-item rate is 8.35%. Also inflates the damaged_in_transit / size_issue training sets via FILTER_MAP (nn/data_builder.py:466-476, REPORT.md:468).

Carried from 2026-09-17, untouched. best_weights is restored at model.py:212 but all_preds/all_targets still hold the final epoch's predictions (reassigned each epoch at model.py:174). Every metric in REPORT.md section 3 therefore describes the discarded final-epoch model while --save_model (nn/estimator.py:527) persists the best checkpoint. With patience=5 the gap is five epochs.

quantity is constant: all 69956 rows in data/line_items.csv have quantity == 1 (verified). get_X_y tests set(unique).issubset({0,1,True,False}); {1} satisfies it, so quantity is typed as a binary task with one class. Training runs to completion against all-ones, then roc_auc_score at model.py:219 raises a bare 'ValueError: Only one class present in y_true'. quantity is advertised as a headline target by _business_line (nn/estimator.py:122) and appears in --list_targets at 100% non-null. It is also a zero-variance dead feature for every other target.

load_and_predict builds the numeric row with float(row.get(col, 0.0)) and then applies the fitted StandardScaler, so an unspecified feature is treated as a genuine zero rather than as missing. Measured at line-item grain from the CSVs, a raw 0.0 default lands at z = -1.55 (price), -1.90 (weight_grams), -1.43 (orders_count), -1.33 (total_spent). The documented example in REFERENCE.md and HOW_TO_USE.md supplies 3 of roughly 56 numeric features, so about 53 arrive as out-of-distribution values. Defaulting to scaler.mean_[i] would scale to exactly 0.

Carried from 2026-09-17, untouched. At --predict time an unseen categorical value falls back to encoder index 0, the alphabetically first real class, with no warning. The unknown-key warning at estimator.py:233 covers a different failure. nn/model.py:40 already allocates vocab_size+1 embedding rows, so a reserved OOV slot exists and is never used.

issues_confirmed.detail: LabelEncoders, the numeric median imputation and the StandardScaler are all fit on the full table inside _encode_and_scale, before train_model performs the train/val split. Validation rows therefore inform the scaling statistics and the category vocabulary. Mild relative to the leakage items, but the same family of problem.
No version pins anywhere, while save_model pickles live sklearn LabelEncoder and StandardScaler objects into the .pkl. A minor sklearn bump silently invalidates every saved model.

No test files exist. validate.py is the vendor dataset reconciler (20 reconciliation rules over the raw CSVs), not a test of anything in nn/. A structural leakage test over every LEAKAGE_MAP key would have caught both the has_refund and has_ticket leaks.

verification_method: Static reading plus stdlib csv/json recounts against data/.
